title: Verbalizing Activation Differences with Natural Language Autoencoders
abstract: arXiv:2610.30934v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Activation verbalizers translate the internal representations of large language models into human-readable text. The recently proposed natural language autoencoders (NLAs) learn this by reconstructing activations through a natural language bottleneck. However, it remains unclear how well these methods generalize beyond the setting they were trained for. Here, we study this question for NLAs along four closely related questions: (i) Do NLA verbalizations exhibit compositional structure with respect to their input? (ii) Do NLAs generalize to finetuned versions of the model they were trained for? (iii) Can NLAs recover finetuning objectives in model diffing? (iv) Can NLAs be specialized for model diffing? Across four models from three families, our experiments provide evidence supporting a largely positive answer to all four questions. translated_title: 用自然语言自编码器将激活差异转化为自然语言描述
translated_abstract: 激活言语化器可以将大语言模型的内部表示翻译成人类可读的文本。最近提出的自然语言自编码器（NLAs）通过自然语言瓶颈重建激活来学习这种转换。然而，这些方法在超出其训练设置的范围外泛化能力如何仍不清楚。本文围绕四个密切相关的问题对NLAs进行研究：（i）NLA的言语化描述对其输入是否表现出组合结构？（ii）NLAs能否泛化到其所训练模型的微调版本？（iii）NLAs能否在模型差异分析中恢复微调目标？（iv）NLAs能否被专门化用于模型差异分析？通过对来自三个系列的四个模型的实验，我们提供的证据支持对这四个问题基本肯定的答案。具体而言，组合类比激活的言语化描述大多能说出目标内容，而很少提及……
tldr: 本文系统研究了自然语言自编码器（NLAs）的泛化能力，实验证明其在组合结构、泛化到微调模型、恢复微调目标以及专门化模型差异分析四个方面均表现良好。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically investigates the generalization of natural language autoencoders (NLAs), showing they exhibit compositional structure, generalize to finetuned models, recover finetuning objectives, and can be specialized for model diffing.
